translations.title: What I Like About the Painting Is That the Dead Man...
translations.text:
What I like about the painting is that the dead man
faces the window and the window
is open and the oxygen
has its way with him, sings and
dances for him, makes him think
of another time, as though lying
there swimming in pallor
were part of his sleeplessness. As for
the roses whose stalks keep growing
outside, among the grass, they sprout
at the speed of his fingernails.

Fan
of the dead.
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: O Voice, Only Voice: All the Hollow of the Sea...
translations.text:
O voice, only voice: all the hollow of the sea,
all the hollow of the sea would not be enough,
all the hollow of the sky,
the whole cavity of beauty
would not be enough to contain you;
and though humanity fell silent and this world sank,
O majesty, you would never,
you would never cease to be everywhere,
for you have time and being to spare, only voice;
for you are and are not, and are almost my God,
and almost my father when I am at my darkest.
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: Football Without End
translations.text:
What a madhouse, World; all things football, balls
and feet, are ranked up to the crest
of Aconcagua: a metaphor
for kicking for its own sake, or a display
of the leather of the Testicle
on the swollen grass, like this: Capital: it ejaculates and
makes whole stadiums ejaculate,
splattering rhetoric and grease
by satellite
in every language, Mayan,
even Etruscan?

To think
there were bullfighters, gladiators
in the contest, and rhythm.
Pindar
would have wept.
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: When I Open the Door of Myself in Objects...
translations.text:
When I open the door of myself in objects:
who steals my blood, what is mine, what is real?
Who hurls me into the void
when I breathe? Who
is my executioner inside myself?

O Time. Many-faced.
Face multiplied by yourself.
Emerge from the origins of music. Emerge
from my weeping. Tear off your laughing mask.
Wait for me to kiss you, convulsive beauty.
Wait for me at the sea's door. Wait for me
in the object I love eternally.
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: Written in Hesiod: There Is No...
translations.text:
Written in Hesiod: There is
no music or submusic beneath the firmament; what there is
is lambada
since Genesis, the stars washed clean
in the open expanse, a mortal man
and a mortal woman, beautiful,
dancing.

And in Guimarães Rosa: A single dancing wrist,
the palms held high instead,
with the scent
of paradise in the science of desire,
a kiss, a chaste
kiss on the nape, danced.

Let us praise the lambada, then, I think,
for being sacred.
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: Darío and More Darío
translations.text:
Star Ogden, accompany me
as she accompanied him; swarm around me
as stars did around Darío; think me
Orphic; accustom me
to being air around
those blind airplanes flying fast in
the proparoxytone New York
to Philadelphia; divine me
in a reversed Tarot with
Nefertitis bleeding beneath
the beauty of
the cloud of what will have been the skin
of hearing you, the
dangerous skin
of this Monday in Berlin with angels;
wherever
you may be, bring me into accord
with another, highest cithara of certainty
whose hypotenuse is God.
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: Lovely Is the Color of This Young Woman’s Hair, Lovely the Scent...
translations.text:
Lovely is the color of this young woman's hair, lovely the bee-like scent
of her humming, lovely the street,
lovely the splendid feet beneath those two
golden shoes, lovely the makeup
from eyelashes to nails, the riverlike flow
of her magnificent arteries, lovely the physis
and metaphysis of her undulation, lovely the meter
seventy of her frame, lovely the pact
between bone and skin, lovely the fullness
of the mother who wove her supple and
slept her through those nine months, lovely the animal
leisure moving within her.
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: Last Night I Touched You and Felt You...
translations.text:
Last night I touched you and felt you
without my hand fleeing beyond my hand,
without my body fleeing, or my ear;
I felt you in a nearly human way.

Pulsing,
I cannot tell whether like blood or a wandering cloud,
through my house, on tiptoe, darkness rising,
darkness falling, you ran, flashing.

You ran through my wooden house,
opened its windows,
and I felt you beat the whole night through,
daughter of the abysses, silent,
warrior, so terrible, so beautiful
that everything that exists,
for me, without your flame, would not exist.
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: Lihn Still Bleeds Too Much to Speak...
translations.text:
Lihn still bleeds too much to speak
of Lihn gone Lihn, “defunctus
adhuc loquitur”; preferable
the absent body of his figure; the burial
does not matter, nor the parable
of the burial's decay: something
that only he and I,
each
in his U-Bahn beneath another
unreal Spree,
each coffin
in its bark,
each nobody
in his nobody, unlubricated
as I go amid the screech
of Berlin's gulls with no
beyond or
this side except in the south
toward the west Adriana,
most sorrowful, Andrea
beneath the drizzle, which
confirms
it all:

Now Lihn
has the floor;
wall
and wall.
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: Some Trees Are Transparent and Know How to Speak...
translations.text:
Some trees are transparent and can speak
several languages at once; others, algebraic,
converse with the air in the grave manner
of stars; others
look like horses and neigh;

among them
are incredible mad types for being motherless;
the chord
of the mist is enough for them.

At night they paint what they see, generate and
divinize another space with another sex unlike
that of Genesis; they sing
and paint at once, more than the craft
of creation, the old craft
of silence

before wonder; they bind the androgynous
net within the weave
of a single body,
tree and resurrected animal,
with the ten thousand senses
we lost at birth;

then
we are another sun.
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.
